plain.li: People have started calling us {GROUP}. I suppose that's what we are now.
Somewhere along the way we became {GROUP}. Nobody decided it. It just happened.
We have our own seats now, and our own jokes. {GROUP}, the others call us.
I heard someone say "{GROUP}" today and realised they meant me too.
It's good to belong to something here. {GROUP}. I like the sound of it.
[groupkind:hunters] We go out together, we come back together. That's what {GROUP} means.
[groupkind:comrades] You don't forget the people who stood beside you. We've become {GROUP} because of it.
[groupkind:nightshift] The night is ours. {GROUP}, they call us, and they're not wrong.
[groupkind:faithful] We pray together now, every day. {GROUP}, the others say, half joking.
[groupkind:founders] We were here first, and we've stayed close. {GROUP}. It fits.

warm.li: I have people here now. {GROUP}. I didn't know how much I needed that.

blunt.li: Apparently I'm one of {GROUP} now. Fine. They're the only ones here worth talking to.

cheerful.li: {GROUP}! We're a proper crowd now. I've half a mind to carve it over the door.

gloomy.li: We're {GROUP} now. I give it a season before something breaks it, but I'll enjoy it while it lasts.

cold.li: The others have taken to calling us {GROUP}. Names are for convenience. Still.

plain.li: I sat with {GROUP} tonight and nobody told me to move. I think I'm one of them now.
{GROUP} have made room for me. I'm still learning the jokes.
I've been spending my evenings with {GROUP}. It feels like the right place.
Someone counted me in when they counted {GROUP} today. I noticed.
[grouprole:newcomer] I'm the new one in {GROUP}. They'll get used to me.

warm.li: {GROUP} took me in without a fuss. I'm grateful, more than I'll tell them.

blunt.li: Started sitting with {GROUP}. Better company than my own.

cheerful.li: One of {GROUP} now. About time, too.

gloomy.li: {GROUP} let me sit with them. I keep waiting for them to change their minds.

plain.li: {GROUP} have taken me in. I'm not the new one any more, not really.
Tonight {GROUP} saved me a seat without being asked. That's when I knew.
It took a while, but I'm one of {GROUP} now.
They told me one of their old stories tonight, the kind they only tell each other. I'm in.
[lowtech] {GROUP} shared their fire with me tonight, and their bread. I'm one of them.
[groupnorm:wary] {GROUP} don't trust easily. They trust me now. I won't let them down.

warm.li: I came here with nothing and no one. Now I have {GROUP}.

blunt.li: {GROUP} finally stopped treating me like a stranger. Took them long enough.

cheerful.li: Officially one of {GROUP}! Well, as official as these things get.

gloomy.li: {GROUP} have let me in. I hope I don't disappoint them.

cold.li: {GROUP} accept me now. It makes things easier.

plain.li: I spoke up for {OTHER_nameDef} with {GROUP}, and now {OTHER_pronoun}'s one of us. Good.
{OTHER_nameDef} is one of {GROUP} now. I told them {OTHER_pronoun} would fit.
I knew {OTHER_nameDef} would settle in with {GROUP}. I just had to get them to see it.

warm.li: {OTHER_nameDef} looked so lost those first days. Now {OTHER_pronoun} has {GROUP}, and I had a hand in it.

blunt.li: Told {GROUP} to give {OTHER_nameDef} a chance. They did. I was right.

plain.li: {GROUP} go quiet when I sit down. I've stopped sitting down.
I tried to join {GROUP} at the fire. Nobody moved up.
{GROUP} have their own jokes and their own seats, and none of them are mine.
They're polite, {GROUP}. Polite the way you are with a stranger.
I don't know what I did to {GROUP}. Maybe nothing. Maybe that's the trouble.
[groupnorm:wary] {GROUP} don't trust anyone new. I'm going to be new for a long time, it seems.
[groupnorm:aloof] {GROUP} keep to themselves, and they mean it.

warm.li: I keep trying with {GROUP}. One day, maybe.

blunt.li: {GROUP} can keep their little club. I don't need it.

cheerful.li: {GROUP} are a tough crowd. I'll win them round, see if I don't.

gloomy.li: I knew it would be like this. It always is, being new.

cold.li: {GROUP} have made their feelings clear. So be it.

plain.li: I don't sit with {GROUP} much any more. I couldn't say when that changed.
{GROUP} have their evenings without me now. I don't think anyone minds, least of all me.
I've drifted away from {GROUP}. We still nod to each other.
Somewhere along the way I stopped being one of {GROUP}.

warm.li: I miss {GROUP}, a little. But I'd stopped fitting.

blunt.li: Done with {GROUP}. We'd nothing left to say to each other.

gloomy.li: {GROUP} went on without me, the way things do.

plain.li: {GROUP} have split. I'm on one side and {OTHER_nameDef} is on the other, and that's that.
We used to be {GROUP}. Now there are two tables where there was one.
It was coming for weeks, and now it's happened: {GROUP} are in two halves.
I don't sit with {OTHER_nameDef} any more. None of us do, on this side.
Everyone in {GROUP} has had to pick a side. I hate it.

warm.li: I keep hoping {GROUP} will mend. I said hello to {OTHER_nameDef} today, at least.

blunt.li: {GROUP} split, and good riddance to the half that left.

cheerful.li: {GROUP} broke apart, but we'll find our feet. We always do.

gloomy.li: I knew {GROUP} couldn't last. Nothing here does.

cold.li: {GROUP} have split. It was inevitable, given who was in it.

plain.li: {OLD} and {GROUP} are one crowd now. The fire's bigger, and so is the noise.
We were sitting with {OLD} most evenings anyway. Now it's official: we're all {GROUP}.
{GROUP} have taken in {OLD}, or the other way round. Nobody can remember which.
More faces round the table now that {OLD} have joined {GROUP}.

warm.li: {OLD} and {GROUP} together. It feels right, like it should always have been this way.

blunt.li: {OLD} are part of {GROUP} now. Fine, as long as they pull their weight.

cheerful.li: Double the stories, double the songs! {OLD} and {GROUP} are one lot now.

gloomy.li: {OLD} joined {GROUP}. More people to lose, I suppose.

plain.li: There's no {GROUP} any more. I walked past our old place by the fire and nobody was there.
I keep thinking about {GROUP}, the way it was at the start.
{GROUP} are no more. Someone should remember us, so I'm writing it down.
We were {GROUP} once. I wonder if anyone else remembers.
[afterraid] So many gone, and {GROUP} with them.

warm.li: I was happy with {GROUP}. I hope the others were too.

blunt.li: That's the end of {GROUP}. It was good while it lasted.

gloomy.li: {GROUP} came apart the way everything does. I'll miss us anyway.

cold.li: It's over for {GROUP}. I find I mind more than I expected.

plain.li: There's an empty seat in {GROUP} tonight. {NAME}'s seat. Nobody will sit in it.
{GROUP} won't be the same without {NAME}. We all know it.
We kept {NAME}'s place at the fire tonight. It seemed right.
{NAME} was the heart of {GROUP} in ways none of us said out loud.
One of {GROUP} is gone. {NAME}. I keep looking round for them.

warm.li: We told stories about {NAME} until late. {GROUP} needed that.

blunt.li: Lost {NAME}. {GROUP} will carry on. That's what you do.

gloomy.li: First {NAME}. Who's next? {GROUP} gets smaller every season.

plain.li: {GROUP} think they run this colony. They don't.
Nobody on our side talks to {GROUP} any more, not if we can help it.
There's bad blood with {GROUP} now. Everyone can feel it at supper.
I don't know who started it with {GROUP}. I know who's going to finish it.
{GROUP} sit at their end and we sit at ours. That's how it is now.

warm.li: I wish it weren't like this with {GROUP}. We used to get on.

blunt.li: {GROUP} can say it to my face, if they've got something to say.

cheerful.li: {GROUP} are sore at us. We'll beat them at cards and see if it helps.

gloomy.li: Two crowds glaring at each other across one colony. It'll end badly.

cold.li: {GROUP} are a nuisance. I've stopped pretending otherwise.

plain.li: All of {GROUP} together tonight, every one of us. It doesn't happen often enough.
{GROUP} sat up late tonight, all of us. I'll remember it.
We made an evening of it, {GROUP} and I. I'm tired and happy.
Somebody called {GROUP} together and everyone came. That says something.

warm.li: An evening with {GROUP}. Exactly what I needed.

cheerful.li: What a night with {GROUP}! My face hurts from laughing.

gloomy.li: A good evening with {GROUP}. Rare enough these days.

plain.li: Not between us. Not over this.
You two sit at the same fire every night. Act like it.
Let it go. You'll laugh about it next week.
Both of you are right, which means both of you are wrong.
Come on, we're all on the same side here.
Say sorry now and it costs you nothing.
Shake on it, and we'll say no more.
[persona:calm] Slowly. One of you, then the other.

warm.li: I hate seeing you two like this. Talk to me.
Nobody here wants this. Least of all you two.

blunt.li: Enough. Save it for the raiders.

cheerful.li: If you're going to fight, at least make it entertaining.

gloomy.li: We've got enough troubles without this.

cold.li: This is beneath both of you.

plain.li: {PAWN_nameDef} got between {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} before it went any further. Nobody quarrels for long in {GROUP}.
{PAWN_nameDef} sat {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} down together and made them hear each other out.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} were at it again until {PAWN_nameDef} came over. It blew over sooner than usual.
{PAWN_nameDef} reminded {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} of the last time they fell out, and how silly it seemed after.
{PAWN_nameDef}, as always in {GROUP}, smoothed things over between {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef}.
{PAWN_nameDef} put a cup in each of their hands and waited until {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} had calmed down.

warm.li: {PAWN_nameDef} talked {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} round, gently, until they were both a little ashamed of themselves.

blunt.li: {PAWN_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} to drop it, and they did.

cheerful.li: {PAWN_nameDef} made a joke of the whole thing, and {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} couldn't keep a straight face.

gloomy.li: {PAWN_nameDef} sighed and stepped between {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef}, as {PAWN_pronoun} so often has to.

cold.li: {PAWN_nameDef} pointed out to {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} exactly how little their quarrel was worth.
